rationale: Retain contract investigation and distinguish unsupported result-buffer mutation from explicitly protected proposal input reuse; do not spend an execution on a scenario whose caller legality is unsettled.

feedback.answered: The synchronous and asynchronous proposal contracts explicitly distinguish timed-out retries from successful completion: on success the client must call ProposalCompleted before future proposals. Therefore obtaining a successful result, mutating its Data and then reissuing the same completed series is not an applicable retry witness. Existing shallow Result.Data propagation remains an observation, but output mutation/retention rights are still unspecified in the inspected Result and GetResult comments; no cache-integrity obligation is inferred from silence. In contrast, the input-byte-slice reuse contract is explicit, and proposalShard.propose passes nonempty commands through preparePayload with nil destination: uncompressed encoding allocates and copies; Snappy encoding creates a copied result. That actual producer establishes independence from later caller input reuse. A separate session-history reading found a sourced preservation expectation: TestOrderedDoIsLRUOrdered and TestLRUSessionCanBeSavedAndRestoredWithLRUOrderPreserved require eviction order preservation. lrusession.save gathers an ordered ID list and serializes in that order; load re-adds in serialized order. Production getSSMeta supplies an in-memory bytes.Buffer for SaveSessions, so an injected failing writer during the snapshot-session serialization would not represent this producer path.
remaining: Result.Data mutation ownership remains unresolved; resume only with a sourced permitted mutation/history that could change an owed result or state, rather than a forbidden completed-series retry.
Inspect other persistence/recovery responsibilities with actual storage and configuration boundaries; do not repeat input-copy or session-order checks merely for coverage.
